comments.author: @Juan_acosta-te2jk
comments.text:
The US (United States) has a proportionally much larger homeless population than Spain. Proportional comparison:

The US has a rate approximately 3–4 times higher than that of Spain.
Harmonized sources (OECD Affordable Housing Database and Our World in Data) confirm the same pattern: Spain ranks among the developed countries with the lowest rates, whereas the US is clearly above that level (with a particularly high proportion of people living on the street).

US: The official 2024 "Point-in-Time" count recorded approximately 771,480 people experiencing homelessness (living on the street or in shelters/transitional housing). This equates to about 23 per 10,000 inhabitants.

Spain: The INE (National Statistics Institute) Survey on Homeless People (2022) counted 28,552 individuals (0.06% of the population). In 2024, the daily average of people accommodated in care centers rose to approximately 33,700–34,100. Organizations such as Hogar Sí or Cáritas estimate the total figure (including those who do not use such centers) at around 37,000–40,000. The rate stands at approximately 6–8 per 10,000 inhabitants.
